Guide.title: Getting Started in Diablo 2 Resurrected
Guide.description: Everything you need to know as a new player. Learn the basics of classes, skills, and progression.
Guide.author: Deckard Cain

content.heading: Installation and Setup
content.text: Diablo 2 Resurrected is available on PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch. The game features full cross-progression, allowing you to carry your characters between platforms as long as you link your Battle.net account.
content.tip: On PC, make sure to check the "Legacy Graphics" toggle (G key) to see the original 2000 graphics in action!

content.heading: The General Game Loop
content.text: The game is divided into five acts. You progress by completing main quests that eventually lead you to the Act Boss. Defeating the boss opens the way to the next act.
list: Act 1: The Rogue Encampment (Andariel)
Act 2: Lut Gholein (Duriel)
Act 3: Kurast (Mephisto)
Act 4: The Pandemonium Fortress (Diablo)
Act 5: Harrogath (Baal)

content.heading: Understanding Difficulties
content.text: The game features three difficulty levels: Normal, Nightmare, and Hell. You must complete the game on one difficulty to unlock the next.
list: Normal: The baseline experience.
Nightmare: Resistances are reduced by 40%. Monsters are stronger.
Hell: Resistances are reduced by 100%. Monsters have immunities to specific damage types.
content.tip: Hell difficulty is where the true endgame begins and the best items in the game can drop.

content.heading: Multiplayer and Trading
content.text: D2R is best enjoyed with others. Lobbies allow you to find games for specific purposes like "Cows", "Baal Runs", or "Trade".
content.text2: Trading is the backbone of the economy. Most players use Runes (like Ber, Jah, or Vex) as the unofficial currency for high-end items.

Guide.title: Class Overview & Comparison
Guide.description: Compare all 7 classes and find the perfect match for your playstyle.
Guide.author: Akara

content.heading: The Seven Heroes
content.text: Diablo 2 features seven distinct classes, each with three unique skill trees. Choosing the right class for your playstyle is the first step to conquering Sanctuary.
list: Amazon: Master of Bows and Javelins. High DPS.
Assassin: Traps and Martial Arts. Versatile and technical.
Necromancer: Summons undead armies and curses enemies. Safe and tactical.
Barbarian: Tanky melee fighter and item finder. Best for buffs (Shouts).
Paladin: Holy warrior with powerful Auras. Best tank/support.
Sorceress: Master of elemental magic. Fastest mobility (Teleport).
Druid: Shapeshifter and elementalist. High survivability.

content.heading: Best Classes for Beginners
content.text: If you are new to the game, some classes are more forgiving than others.
content.tip: The Summon Necromancer and Trap Assassin are widely considered the safest builds for a first playthrough due to their ability to deal damage without being in melee range.

Guide.title: Your First Character Guide
Guide.description: Step-by-step guide on building your first character from level 1 to Hell.
Guide.author: Charsi

content.heading: Picking a Starter
content.text: Your first character has one main job: to find gear for your other characters. You want a build that functions well with very little equipment.
list: Sorceress (Blizzard/HydraOrb): Free Teleport makes farming fast.
Paladin (Hammerdin): High damage output with low gear requirements.

content.heading: Stat Allocation Basics
content.text: For almost every character, the stat allocation strategy is the same:
list: Strength: Enough to wear gear.
Dexterity: Enough for Max Block (Paladin) or Gear (others).
Vitality: EVERYTHING ELSE. Life is survival.
Energy: Usually 0. Use potions for mana.

Guide.title: Normal, Nightmare, Hell Explained
Guide.description: Understanding difficulty modes, resistance penalties, and monster immunities.
Guide.author: Warriv

content.heading: The Resistance Penalties
content.text: As you advance difficulties, your resistances take a massive hit. You must compensate with gear.
list: Normal: 0% Penalty
Nightmare: -40% Penalty
Hell: -100% Penalty
content.tip: Entering Hell with negative Fire/Lightning resistance is a death sentence. Prioritize 'Smoke' runeword or 'Ancients Pledge' shield.

content.heading: Monster Immunities
content.text: In Hell difficulty, nearly every monster is 'Immune' to at least one element (Fire, Cold, Lightning, Poison, Physical, or Magic). This means they take 0 damage from that source.
content.text2: You must either skip these monsters (Teleport), rely on your Mercenary to kill them, or use a dual-element build.

Guide.title: Item Basics: Rarities & Affixes
Guide.description: Learn about item qualities from white to unique, and how affixes work.
Guide.author: Gheed

content.heading: Item Quality Tiers
content.text: Items come in several colors indicating their rarity and function.
list: White/Grey: Base items. Used for Runewords.
Blue (Magic): 1-2 random stats. Can have very high rolls.
Yellow (Rare): 2-6 random stats. Can be best-in-slot.
Gold (Unique): Fixed stats with some variance. Unique names and art.
Green (Set): Fixed stats. Grants bonuses when wearing multiple pieces.
Orange (Crafted): Created in the Cube. Fixed stats + random stats.

content.heading: Prefixes and Suffixes
content.text: Magic and Rare items are built from Affixes. A 'Prefix' adds a name to the start (e.g. 'Cruel') and a 'Suffix' adds to the end (e.g. 'of Quickness').
content.tip: A 'Cruel Colossus Blade of Quickness' combines high damage % (Cruel) with Attack Speed (Quickness).

Guide.title: Breakpoints Explained (FCR/FHR/IAS)
Guide.description: The complete guide to cast rate, hit recovery, and attack speed breakpoints.
Guide.author: Kashya

content.heading: What are Breakpoints?
content.text: Diablo 2 runs at 25 frames per second. Animations like casting spells, swinging weapons, or recovering from a hit take a certain number of frames. Breakpoints are the specific values of stats (FCR/FHR/IAS) required to reduce the number of frames an animation takes.
content.tip: If you have 104% FCR and the next breakpoint is at 105%, you still cast as if you have 63% FCR. Every point matters only when you hit the threshold!

content.heading: Faster Cast Rate (FCR)
content.text: FCR reduces the time it takes to cast a spell. This is crucial for builds like Hammerdins, Sorceresses, and Wind Druids.
list: Sorceress (Standard): 37, 63, 105, 200
Paladin (Standard): 48, 75, 125
Druid (Human): 46, 68, 99, 163
Necromancer: 48, 75, 125

content.heading: Faster Hit Recovery (FHR)
content.text: FHR determines how quickly your character recovers after taking a "hit" that deals more than 1/12th of your total health. High FHR prevents you from being "locked" in a hit-stun animation.
list: Sorc/Necro/Druid (Human): 42, 60, 86, 142
Paladin/Barb/Amazon: 48, 86, 200
content.tip: In PvP or when surrounded by fast-attacking mobs (like Moon Lords), hitting the 86% FHR breakpoint is often a life-saver.

Guide.title: Skill Synergies Guide
Guide.description: How synergies work and maximizing your damage output.
Guide.author: Ormus

content.heading: What are Synergies?
content.text: Synergies are bonuses that skills receive from points placed in OTHER skills. For example, Fireball receives a damage bonus from Fire Bolt and Meteor.
content.tip: Only 'Hard Points' (points you actually click to invest) count for Synergies! +Skills from gear DO NOT increase Synergy bonuses.

content.heading: Masteries vs Synergies
content.text: Sorceress Masteries (Fire/Lightning) apply to the total damage. Synergies are usually additive with each other, then multiplied by the Mastery.
content.text2: Cold Mastery is unique; it reduces enemy resistance instead of adding damage %.

Guide.title: Magic Find Deep Dive
Guide.description: How MF affects drops, diminishing returns, and optimal MF values.
Guide.author: Elzix

content.heading: How Magic Find Works
content.text: Magic Find (MF) increases the chance of an item being Magic, Rare, Set, or Unique. However, it does not affect the base item type or the chance of finding Runes.
content.tip: Runes are not affected by MF. To find more runes, focus on clear speed and density (like the Cow Level) rather than stacking MF.

content.heading: Diminishing Returns
content.text: While MF is critical, it suffers from significant diminishing returns for Uniques and Sets. Going from 0 to 200 MF is a huge boost, but going from 600 to 800 MF is barely noticeable.
content.tip: Aim for a 250-400 MF "sweet spot" where you can still clear content quickly.

Guide.title: Resistances & Absorb Guide
Guide.description: Understanding max res, absorb, and damage reduction mechanics.
Guide.author: Fara

content.heading: Resistance Cap
content.text: Resistances are capped at 75% by default. This can be raised to 95% using items like 'Guardian Angel' or 'Thundergods Vigor'.
content.tip: Increasing your max resistance from 75% to 90% reduces incoming damage by 60%! It is a massive defensive layer.

content.heading: Absorb
content.text: Absorb heals you for a portion of the element received. % Absorb applies first, then Flat Absorb. It is possible to heal from attacks if you have enough Absorb.

Guide.title: Crushing Blow & Deadly Strike
Guide.description: How these powerful combat mechanics work and when to stack them.
Guide.author: Greiz

content.heading: Crushing Blow (CB)
content.text: CB reduces a monster's current health by a percentage (25% for normal mobs, 12.5% for Bosses). It is mandatory for killing Act Bosses and Ubers quickly.
content.tip: Static Field acts similarly to Crushing Blow for Sorceresses.

content.heading: Deadly Strike (DS)
content.text: DS is a chance to deal double damage. It is crucial for physical builds like Bowazons and Zealots.
content.text2: Critical Strike (Amazon/Barbarian skill) does the same thing. They don't stack linearly; they are rolled independently.

Guide.title: Area Levels & Monster Levels
Guide.description: Understanding alvl, mlvl, and how they affect drops.
Guide.author: Drognan

content.heading: Area Level (alvl)
content.text: In Hell difficulty, the Area Level determines the level of the items that can drop. 'Level 85 Areas' (TC87) are famous because they can drop EVERY unique item in the game.
list: The Pit (Act 1)
Ancient Tunnels (Act 2)
Chaos Sanctuary (Act 4)
Worldstone Keep (Act 5)

Guide.title: The Pit Farming Guide
Guide.description: Complete guide to farming The Pit including routes, builds, and drop rates.
Guide.author: Lysander

content.heading: Why Farm the Pit?
content.text: The Pit is a "Level 85 Area" located in the Tamoe Highland in Act 1. This means that every unique item in the game, including elite weapons and armors, can drop here.
content.tip: It is one of the most accessible Level 85 areas for early endgame characters.

content.heading: How to Find the Pit
content.text: Take the Outer Cloister waypoint in Act 1. Follow the road into the Tamoe Highland. The road will eventually split; one path leads to the Monastery, and the other leads directly to the Pit entrance.

content.heading: Monster Immunities
content.text: The Pit contains monsters with various immunities, making it important to choose the right build.
list: Skeletal Mages: Lightning Immune
Devilkin: Fire Immune
Dark Archers: Lightning Immune
Dark Stalkers: Cold Immune
content.tip: Physical and Magic damage builds (like Hammerdins or Wind Druids) excel here due to fewer immunities.

content.heading: Efficiency Tips
content.text: Focus on killing Champion and Unique packs. These have the highest chance to drop high-level uniques and runes. Level 2 of the Pit is small but contains a glittering chest and several guaranteed boss packs.

Guide.title: Ancient Tunnels Guide
Guide.description: No cold immunes make this perfect for Blizzard Sorcs.
Guide.author: Hratli

content.heading: The Cold Sorc Paradise
content.text: The Ancient Tunnels (Lost City, Act 2) is a Level 85 Area that naturally spawns with NO Cold Immune monsters (except occasional unique bosses). This makes it the #1 farming spot for Blizzard Sorceresses.
content.tip: Unlike The Pit, you don't need Enigma or high-end gear here. A budget Sorc can clear it safely.

Guide.title: Chaos Sanctuary Routes
Guide.description: Optimal pathing and builds for efficient Chaos runs.
Guide.author: Tyrael

content.heading: The Chaos Sanctuary
content.text: Located in the heart of Hell (Act 4), the Chaos Sanctuary is home to Diablo and some of the most dangerous monsters in the game. It is a Level 85 area, meaning every unique can drop here.
content.tip: Seal popping is a common strategy to clear the screen instantly, but be careful—monsters only drop loot if you've "seen" them in the last few seconds!

content.heading: The Three Seals
content.text: To spawn Diablo, you must activate five seals and defeat the three boss packs they spawn: Lord De Seis, Grand Vizier of Chaos, and Infector of Souls.
list: West Seals: Grand Vizier (Extra Fast Fire Immune)
North Seals: Lord De Seis (Extra Strong Fire/Cold Immune)
East Seals: Infector of Souls (Extra Fast Fire Immune)

Guide.title: Secret Cow Level Guide
Guide.description: How to access cows, best builds, and rune farming strategies.
Guide.author: The Cow King

content.heading: The Secret Cow Level
content.text: Moo! The Secret Cow Level is legendary for its massive density of Hell Bovines. It is the best place in the game to find high-quality white base items for runewords and high runes.
content.tip: In D2R, you can now kill the Cow King as many times as you want without losing access to the portal!

content.heading: How to Access
content.text: To open the portal, you must first finish the Baal quest in the current difficulty. Then, go to Tristram in Act 1 and find Wirt's Body to get Wirt's Leg.
list: Go to Stony Field Act 1
Enter Red Portal to Tristram
Find Wirt's Body (Top Left)
Transmute Wirt's Leg + Tome of Town Portal in Rogue Encampment

content.heading: Build Recommendations
content.text: The best builds for Cows are those with high Area of Effect (AoE) damage and clear speed.
list: Javazon (Lightning Fury): The undisputed queen of cows.
Corpse Explosion Necromancer: Uses cow density against itself.
Blizzard Sorceress: Excellent for kiting and freezing groups.

Guide.title: Countess Rune Farming
Guide.description: Efficient Countess farming for early-mid runes.
Guide.author: Jamella

content.heading: The Countess and Runes
content.text: The Countess has a special "Rune Drop" table that bypasses standard drop mechanics, making her the most consistent source for runes up to Ist (Hell difficulty).
content.tip: In Hell difficulty, the Countess can drop up to Lo from her standard table, but she only drops up to Ist from her special rune table.

content.heading: Efficient Pathing: Left-Turn Rule
content.text: To find the stairs quickly, always turn left relative to the direction your character entered the floor. This rule applies to all five levels of the Forgotten Tower.
content.tip: Wait, the rule is "left relative to the shield arm" or "clockwise". Turning left consistently is the fastest way down.

Guide.title: Travincal Gold & HR Farming Guide
Guide.description: The ultimate guide to Council farming for High Runes, Jewelry, and millions of Gold.
Guide.author: Alkor

content.heading: Why Farm Travincal?
content.text: Travincal is widely considered one of the absolute best farming locations in Diablo 2 Resurrected. It boasts high density of 'Super Unique' monsters (the High Council) that have an excellent drop rate for High Runes (up to Cham), Jewels, and Charms.
content.text2: In addition to HRs, Council members drop massive amounts of gold, which is essential if you want to gamble for top-tier circlets, rings, and amulets at Gheed or Anya.
list: High Rune Potential: High drop chances for runes like Sur, Lo, Ber, Jah, and Cham.
Gold Farming: With gold-find gear, you can regularly pull hundreds of thousands of gold in a single 1-minute run.
Efficiency: The waypoint is directly beside the Council, meaning run times are extremely short.
content.tip: Magic Find (MF) does NOT affect the drop rate of Runes. If you are specifically hunting runes, prioritize Kill Speed over MF gear!

content.heading: Top Build Choices
content.text: Because the Council naturally spawns with specific immunities and deals high elemental damage, you need a specialized build.
list: Find Item Barbarian ('Horker'): The absolute king. The 'Find Item' skill allows you to pop every corpse a second time, effectively doubling your loot every run.
Hammerdin: Incredibly safe and efficient since Council members are rarely Magic Immune. High survivability allows for easy clears.
Blizzard Sorceress: Fast runs with teleport, provided you can handle or skip Cold Immune spawns (or use a Sunder Charm).

content.heading: Handling Council Mechanics & Dangers
content.text: The High Council members frequently spam Hydras and often spawn with Conviction auras. High Fire resistance (and ideally fire absorb) is practically mandatory to survive.
list: Toorc Icefist: Always Cold Immune and Stoneskin.
Ismail Vilehand: Always Fire Immune and Extra Fast.
Geleb Flamefinger: Always Fire and Lightning Immune, Extra Strong.
content.tip: Equipping a Dwarf Star ring gives you Fire Absorb, effectively turning Hydra damage into healing. Cannot Be Frozen is also required for any melee builds fighting the Council!

content.heading: Mercenary Care
content.text: Your Act 2 mercenary will die instantly to Hydras if unprepared. Give them gear with +Max Fire Resist (like Guardian Angel armor), Life Leech, and decent damage to survive the onslaught.

Guide.title: Comprehensive Terror Zone Farming
Guide.description: Unlock level 99 quickly and find every item in the game with this Terror Zone mastery guide.
Guide.author: Hadriel

content.heading: What are Terror Zones?
content.text: Terror Zones (TZ) are hourly rotating events that empower specific areas in Sanctuary. Monsters in a Terror Zone scale their level based on the game creator's level.
content.text2: This makes them the most efficient source of Experience and high-end Loot in the entire game, allowing players to reach Level 99 without mindlessly grinding Baal thousands of times.
list: Normal Monsters: Player Level + 2 (Capped at 96)
Champion Monsters: Player Level + 4 (Capped at 98)
Unique/Super Unique/Bosses: Player Level + 5 (Capped at 99)

content.heading: Unlocking and Tracking TZs
content.text: To participate in a Terror Zone for a specific difficulty, you must have defeated Baal on that character and difficulty (Normal, Nightmare, or Hell).
content.tip: You can check which zone is currently Terrorized by looking at the in-game chat window or observing the purple text next to a waypoint.

content.heading: Sunder Charms
content.text: Hell difficulty Terror Zones are the ONLY place in Diablo 2 Resurrected where 'Sunder Charms' can drop. These powerful Grand Charms break monster immunities (capping their resistance at 95%), which opens up previously unviable builds for endgame farming.

content.heading: S-Tier Terror Zones to Farm
content.text: Not all Terror Zones are created equal. Focus on zones with high density and elite packs.
list: Chaos Sanctuary (Act 4): S-Tier. Incredible density, great layouts, and boss drops from Diablo.
Worldstone Keep / Throne of Destruction (Act 5): S-Tier. The highest baseline level area becomes even better. Astounding XP and drops.
Tal Rasha's Tombs (Act 2): S-Tier. Unmatched monster density. Clearing all 7 tombs is extremely rewarding.
The Secret Cow Level (Act 1): S-Tier. Huge density for high rune hunting.
The Pit (Act 1): A-Tier. Always highly efficient, with even better drops when Terrorized.

content.heading: Farming Efficiency
content.text: When a terrible Terror Zone appears (like Maggot Lair or Blood Moor), don't force yourself to farm it. It's often better to go back to standard boss runs (Mephisto, Pindleskin) or just log off and wait for the next hour's rotation. Efficiency is key to D2R wealth!

Guide.title: Trading Basics & Etiquette
Guide.description: Learn the fundamentals of D2R trading and common practices.
Guide.author: Gheed

content.heading: How to Trade
content.text: Most trading happens in game lobbies (e.g. 'O Shako N Ist') or on third-party sites like Traderie or JSP. Always keep your trade window clear and double check items.
content.tip: Mouse over every item before clicking Accept!

content.heading: Common Terms
list: O: Offer (what I have)
N: Need (what I want)
Bin: Buy It Now price
C/O: Current Offer

Guide.title: Rune Value Guide
Guide.description: Current rune prices and exchange rates for the ladder.
Guide.author: Malah

content.heading: The Economy of Runes
content.text: High Runes (HR) are the universal currency of Diablo 2. Because of their rarity and utility in powerful runewords like Enigma or Infinity, their value remains high throughout the ladder season.
content.tip: A "Ber" rune is often the baseline for measuring the value of top-tier items.

content.heading: Mid-Tier Value Runes
content.text: Runes from Pul to Ist are commonly used for mid-level trading. They are frequent enough to be found by dedicated farmers but rare enough to hold significant trade value.
list: Ist: The "standard" for mid-tier items.
Mal/Um/Pul: used for smaller upgrades or bulk trades.
Lem: Highly valued for the "Wealth" and "Treasure" runewords.

Guide.title: How to Price Items
Guide.description: Learn what makes items valuable and how to evaluate gear.
Guide.author: Larzuk

content.heading: Key Value Factors
content.text: Three things determine value: Supply (Rarity), Demand (Utility), and Perfection (Stats). An item must be USEFUL to be valuable.
list: Sockets: Ethereal Armors MUST have 4 sockets (bugged no longer exist in D2R) for Fortitude.
Resistances: Anything under max roll is worth significantly less.
Life/Mana: High rolls on charms are exponential in value.

Guide.title: Avoiding Scams & Safe Trading
Guide.description: Common scam tactics and how to trade safely.
Guide.author: Asheara

content.heading: The Oldest Trick: The Swap
content.text: A scammer will put a valuable item in the window (like Shako), then close it saying 'inventory full'. They reopen and put a look-alike item (green cap with gem) in. ALWAYS check the item after the window reopens.

content.heading: The Corpse Pop
content.text: They ask you to drop an item, claiming they can dupe it. Then they kill you or have a friend kill you to steal it. NEVER drop items on the ground.

Guide.title: Uber Tristram Complete Guide
Guide.description: Everything about Ubers: keys, organs, builds, and Torch farming.
Guide.author: Qual-Kehk

content.heading: The Keys of Terror, Hate, and Destruction
content.text: To enter Uber Tristram, you must first collect three sets of three keys from specific bosses in Hell difficulty. Transmute these keys in Harrogath (Act 5) to open portals to three mini-ubers.
list: Key of Terror: Dropped by The Countess (Black Marsh)
Key of Hate: Dropped by The Summoner (Arcane Sanctuary)
Key of Destruction: Dropped by Nihlathak (Halls of Vaught)

content.heading: The Mini-Ubers and Organs
content.text: Opening the three portals will lead you to Izual, Lilith, and Duriel. Defeating them grants you the Organs needed to open the final portal to Uber Tristram.
list: Mephistos Brain (Izual)
Diablos Horn (Lilith)
Baals Eye (Duriel)
content.tip: Lilith is widely considered the most dangerous of the mini-ubers due to her high poison damage and physical power.

content.heading: The Final Stand: Uber Tristram
content.text: Once you have the three Organs, transmute them in Harrogath to open the portal to the burnt-out husk of Tristram. There, you must face Uber Mephisto, Uber Baal, and Uber Diablo simultaneously.
content.tip: Separate them! Drag Mephisto away first. His Conviction aura is the deadliest mechanic in the fight.

content.heading: Essential Mechanics: Life Tap and Crushing Blow
content.text: To defeat Ubers, you need specialized gear. Almost every successful Uber build relies on Life Tap for survival and Crushing Blow to shred their massive health pools.
list: Life Tap: Heals you for a portion of the damage dealt. Found on Dracul's Grasp or Exile Shield.
Crushing Blow: Deals a percentage of the enemy's remaining health. Essential for the first 90% of the fight.

Guide.title: Diablo Clone (DClone) Guide
Guide.description: How to spawn and defeat Uber Diablo for Anni.
Guide.author: Marius

content.heading: The Annihilus Charm
content.text: The Annihilus (Anni) is a unique Small Charm that gives +1 All Skills, Attributes, Resistances, and XP Gain. It drops only from Uber Diablo.
content.tip: Only one Anni can be carried at a time.

content.heading: Spawning DClone
content.text: DClone spawns when a certain number of Stone of Jordan (SOJ) rings are sold to vendors on the server region. When the message 'Diablo Walks the Earth' appears, the NEXT Super Unique monster you spawn (e.g. Rakanishu, Eldritch) will be replaced by Uber Diablo.

Guide.title: Pandemonium Event Walkthrough
Guide.description: Step-by-step guide to farming Hellfire Torch.
Guide.author: Halbu

content.heading: The Quest for the Torch
content.text: The Pandemonium Event is the only way to obtain the Hellfire Torch Large Charm. It is the pinnacle of Diablo 2 endgame content.
list: Step 1: Collect 3x3 Keys
Step 2: Open 3 Portals to Mini-Ubers
Step 3: Collect 3 Organs
Step 4: Open Final Portal to Uber Tristram
content.tip: Never open all three portals on top of each other! Open them in different spots in Act 5 town to avoid portal overlap.

Guide.title: Level 99 Grind Guide
Guide.description: Optimal XP routes and strategies for reaching 99.
Guide.author: Nihlathak

content.heading: The Climb
content.text: Reaching level 99 is one of the hardest grinds in gaming. From level 98 to 99 alone takes longer than 1-98.
content.tip: The fastest way is Terror Zones (Player 8). Before Terror Zones, only Diablo, Baal, and Nihlathak gave XP at 98.

content.heading: Strategies
list: Always run with an 'Experience Shrine' if possible.
Use an Annihilus charm (+10% XP).
Ondal's Wisdom staff gives +5% XP.

Guide.title: Runeword Basics
Guide.description: How to make runewords: rules, bases, and common mistakes.
Guide.author: Charsi

content.heading: The Golden Rules
content.text: To successfully make a runeword, you must:
list: 1. Use a Grey item (White item with sockets). Magic/Rare/Unique items DO NOT work.
2. Have the EXACT number of sockets (3 rune word needs 3 sockets).
3. Insert runes in the EXACT order.
4. Use the correct item type (e.g. 'Spirit' works in Sword/Shield, not Helm).
content.tip: If you fail, use Hel Rune + TP Scroll in the Cube to wipe the sockets clean (destroying the runes).

Guide.title: Crafting Recipes Guide
Guide.description: All crafting recipes: Blood, Caster, Hit Power, and Safety.
Guide.author: Alkor

content.heading: The Art of Crafting
content.text: Crafting uses the Horadric Cube to create "Orange" items with fixed and variable stats. These can often be Best-in-Slot for specific builds.
content.tip: Caster Amulets are the most sought-after craft, with the potential for +2 Skills and 20% Faster Cast Rate.

content.heading: Common Recipes
content.text: Here are the most frequently used crafting recipes for endgame equipment.
list: Caster Amulet: Ral Rune + Perfect Amethyst + Jewel + Mag. Amulet
Blood Ring: Sol Rune + Perfect Ruby + Jewel + Mag. Ring
Hit Power Gloves: Ort Rune + Perfect Sapphire + Jewel + Mag. Chain Gloves

Guide.title: Socket Recipes & Bases
Guide.description: Cube recipes for adding sockets and best bases for runewords.
Guide.author: Larzuk

content.heading: Adding Sockets (Larzuk vs Cube)
content.text: Larzuk (Act 5 Quest 1) always adds the MAXIMUM number of sockets a white item can hold. The Horadric Cube recipe rolls a random number of sockets (1 to Max).
content.tip: Use Larzuk for guaranteed outcomes (like Crystal Sword -> 4 Sockets from Normal Cows).

content.heading: Cube Recipe
content.text: Ral Rune + Amn Rune + Perfect Amethyst + Normal Weapon = Socketed Weapon (Random Sockets)
content.text2: Tal + Thul + PTopaz + Body Armor = Socketed Armor

Guide.title: Upgrade Recipes Guide
Guide.description: Upgrading uniques and rares from Normal to Exceptional to Elite.
Guide.author: Halbu

content.heading: Upgrading Items
content.text: You can upgrade the 'Base Type' of Unique and Rare items to increase defense or damage. This increases requirements (Str/Dex/Lvl).
list: Unique Normal -> Exceptional Weapon: Ral + Sol + PEmerald
Unique Exceptional -> Elite Weapon: Lum + Pul + PEmerald (Ladder Only in original, D2R unlocked)
Unique Normal -> Exceptional Armor: Tal + Shael + PDiamond
Unique Exceptional -> Elite Armor: Ko + Lem + PDiamond

Guide.title: Speed Leveling 1-80 Guide
Guide.description: Fastest leveling route through all three difficulties.
Guide.author: Flavie

content.heading: The 1-80 Journey
content.text: Reaching level 80 quickly requires a balance of questing and repetitive farming in high-density areas. This route is designed to get you to Hell difficulty as fast as possible.
content.tip: Do not stay in one difficulty too long. Move to the next as soon as you meet the level requirements and your resistances allow.

content.heading: Level 1-25: Early Normal
content.text: Focus on clearing Act 1 and Act 2. Tristram and Tal Rasha's Tombs are the best spots for bulk XP in the early game.
list: Level 1-15: Tristram Runs
Level 15-20: Tal Rasha's Tombs
Level 20-24: Cow Level (Normal)
Level 24-25: Ancients (Act 5)

content.heading: Level 25-45: Baal Runs (Normal)
content.text: Between levels 25 and 40, Baal runs in Normal difficulty provide the fastest experience. Once you hit 40, you should complete the Baal quest and move to Nightmare.
content.tip: If you can join a group, "Baal-01", "Baal-02" games are the gold standard for efficiency.

Guide.title: Classic Leveling Route
Guide.description: Tombs, Baal, Chaos - the classic path to high levels.
Guide.author: Meshif

content.heading: Legacy Route
content.text: Before Terror Zones, the route was simple: Tristram > Tombs > Cows > Baal. Repeat in Nightmare/Hell.
content.tip: The Ancients quest gives a massive XP bump (1 level usually) but gatekeeps Baal runs. Save it until you hit the level cap for the previous act.

Guide.title: Solo Self-Found Leveling
Guide.description: Tips for leveling without trading or rushing.
Guide.author: Geglash

content.heading: Survival First
content.text: In SSF (Solo Self Found), you cannot rely on trading for gear. You must farm it.
list: Farm 'Stealth' (Tal+Eth) armor early.
Farm 'Spirit' runes in NM Countess.
Shop for Resists/Life belts and gloves.

Guide.title: Power Leveling & Rushing
Guide.description: Getting rushed and power-leveled efficiently.
Guide.author: Jerhyn

content.heading: The Grush (Glitch Rush)
content.text: A level 1 character can be rushed to Hell difficulty if they party with a level 40 character who needs the Baal Quest. This character (the 'bumper') completes the quest, and the level 1 character gets credit.
content.tip: Once in Hell, the level 1 character can level in Chaos Sanctuary runs ('Chaos Leech') from 1 to 60 in just a few hours.

Guide.title: Valuable Magic Items
Guide.description: Blue items that are worth a fortune. Don't leave these on the ground!
Guide.author: Anya

content.heading: Why Magic (Blue) Items?
content.text: Magic items can roll specific affixes that Rares, Uniques, and Runewords cannot. Specifically, they can have the highest possible values for certain stats (like 4 sockets on a shield with block chance, or +6 skills on a class item).
content.tip: Always pick up blue Monarchs, Javelins, and Druid Pelts!

content.heading: The Holy Grails of Blue Items
content.text: These are some of the most valuable items in the entire game, often worth multiple High Runes.
list: JMOD (Jeweler's Monarch of Deflecting): 4 Sockets + 30% Faster Block / 20% Block Chance. The ultimate shield for Facets.
6/40 Javelins: +6 Javelin Skills + 40% Increased Attack Speed. Best in Slot for pure lightning fury output.
Jeweler's Archon Plate of the Whale: 4 Sockets + up to 100 Life. Premier PvP armor.
3/20 Gloves: +3 Java/Bow Skills + 20% IAS gloves. Shop these at Anya!

content.heading: Valuable Charms
content.text: Magic charms are the primary source of inventory power.
list: Skiller Grand Charms with +40-45 Life
Small Charms: 3 Max Dmg / 20 AR / 20 Life (3/20/20)
Small Charms: 5 All Res / 20 Life
Small Charms: 7% Magic Find / 11% Fire Res

Guide.title: Valuable Unique & Set Items
Guide.description: Which Uniques are actually worth keeping? A guide to high-value drops.
Guide.author: Deckard Cain

content.heading: Perfect Rolls Matter
content.text: Many unique items are worthless with low stats but incredibly valuable with perfect rolls. Always check the variable stats!
list: Griffon's Eye: -20% Enemy Lightning Res / +15% Lightning Dmg is the goal.
Death's Fathom: +30% Cold Dmg is massive.
Crown of Ages: 2 Sockets is mandatory for high value. 15% DR / 30 All Res is perfect.
Eschuta's Temper: +3 Skills / +20% Fire or Lightning.

content.heading: The Ultra Rares (TC87)
content.text: These items drop only from the highest level monsters and are trophy items.
list: Death's Web: The Holy Grail for Poison Necromancers. +2 Skills / -50% Poison Res is perfect.
Tyrael's Might: The rarest item in the game. Mostly a collector's piece.
Mang Song's Lesson: Extremely rare, though often outclassed by runewords.

content.heading: Valuable Set Items
content.text: Most set items are common, but a few carry significant value.
list: Tal Rasha's Guardianship (Armor): Early ladder wealth.
Tal Rasha's Adjudication (Amulet): Always useful.
Immortal King's Soul Cage (Armor): Rare drop, essential for the full set.

Guide.title: High Value Base Items
Guide.description: White and Grey items that are the foundation of powerful Runewords.
Guide.author: Charsi

content.heading: Elite Armors
content.text: For armors, we generally look for 3 sockets (Enigma) or 4 sockets (Fortitude). "Superior" bases with Enhanced Defense (ED) increase value significantly.
list: Archon Plate: 3 Sockets, Superior 15% ED (Enigma base)
Mage Plate: 3 Sockets, Superior 15% ED (Enigma base - low str req)
Sacred Armor: Ethereal (Mercenary Fortitude base)

content.heading: Elite Weapons
content.text: Mercenary weapons and specific runeword bases are always in demand.
list: Thresher / Giant Thresher: Ethereal, 4 Sockets (Infinity base). Fast attack speed is key.
Berserker Axe: 5 Sockets (Grief) or 6 Sockets (Breath of the Dying).
Phase Blade: 5 Sockets (Grief). Superior 15% ED represents max damage.

content.heading: Class Specific Bases
content.text: Paladin Shields and other class items can be worth more than the runewords put into them.
list: Sacred Targe / Vortex Shield: Ethereal or Non-Eth with +45 All Resistances (Spirit/Exile base).
Grand Matron Bow: +3 Bow Skills, 4 Sockets (Faith base).

Guide.title: Valuable Rare Items
Guide.description: Yellow items with the potential to outclass everything else. Learn what rolls to keep.
Guide.author: Alkor

content.heading: Why Rare Items?
content.text: Rare items can have up to 6 affixes (3 prefixes and 3 suffixes). While they often roll poorly, a Godly rare circlet, ring, or pair of boots can be the most valuable item on the server.
content.tip: Rare items are the ultimate endgame chase. A perfect rare is statistically much harder to find than any unique.

content.heading: Rare Circlets & Coronets
content.text: The gold standard for rare headgear. Look for the 2/20/30 combination.
list: 2/20/30: +2 Class Skills, 20% Faster Cast Rate, 30% Faster Run/Walk.
Sockets: 2 Sockets (via natural roll) adds astronomical value.
Adds: Strength, Dexterity, and All Resistances are the preferred secondary stats.

content.heading: Rare Tactical Boots (Tri-Res)
content.text: High-end boots are defined by their resistance totals and utility stats.
list: Tri-Res: 30% FRW + 10% FHR + 30%+ Fire/Lightning/Cold Resistances.
MF Boots: Rare boots can also roll up to 25% Magic Find alongside resistances.

content.heading: Rare Rings & Amulets
content.text: Jewelry offers the most compact source of stats in the game.
list: Dual Leech Rings: Life Leech + Mana Leech + Strength/Dexterity + Resistances.
FCR Rings: 10% FCR + High Strength/Dexterity + All Resistances.
+2 Skills Amulets: Rare amulets can have +2 Class Skills, though they are often outclassed by Crafted Caster amulets (which can hit 20% FCR).

Guide.title: Advanced Combat Mechanics: CB, DS, & OW
Guide.description: A deep dive into Crushing Blow, Deadly Strike, and Open Wounds for physical damage builds.
Guide.author: Nexus Team

content.heading: Crushing Blow (CB)
content.text: Crushing Blow reduces a target's current health by a percentage. It is essential for taking down high-health bosses like Ubers.
list: Normal Monsters: 1/4 Life reduction.
Bosses/Champions: 1/8 Life reduction.
Players/Mercenaries: 1/10 Life reduction.
Note: Reached via items like Guillaume's Face, Gore Rider, and Grief (indirectly via speed).

content.heading: Deadly Strike (DS) & Critical Strike (CS)
content.text: Both Deadly Strike and Critical Strike provide a chance to deal double physical damage. They do NOT stack to triple damage; the game checks for one, then the other.
list: Deadly Strike: From gear (Highlord's Wrath, Grief).
Critical Strike: From skills (Amazon/Barbarian skills).
Formula: Chance = DS + (CS * (1 - DS/100))

content.heading: Open Wounds (OW)
content.text: Open Wounds causes the target to bleed over time, preventing monster regeneration.
list: Duration: Always 8 seconds (200 frames).
Damage: Scales with Character Level.
Essential for: Prevent Monster Heal on Ubers where regular health regen is massive.

Guide.title: Gambling Strategy Masterclass
Guide.description: How to efficiently gamble for GG items and the legendary Gull Dagger trick.
Guide.author: Nexus Team

content.heading: The Gull Dagger Trick
content.text: The Gull Dagger (100% MF) is an incredible early-game item. You can gamble it easily with a low-level character.
list: Character Level: Use a Level 11 character.
Item: Gamble for 'Dagger' (not Dirks or Poignards).
Logic: At Level 11, the game has the highest probability of rolling the unique Gull Dagger relative to other rare/magic affixes.

content.heading: High Level Gambling
content.text: For end-game gambling (Circlets, Rings, Amulets), specific character levels unlock the best outcomes.
list: Level 93+: The magic number for Amulets. Guarantees every amulet is iLvl 88+, which can roll +2 To Class Skills.
Level 87+: Optimal for gambling Coronets to hit +2 Skills.
Level 44-58: Good range for target-farming specific mid-level unique rings like SOJ (Stone of Jordan) or Nagelring.

content.heading: Efficiency Tips
content.text: Gambling is about volume. Use the 'Refresh' button spam and Edge Bow.
list: Edge Runeword (Tir+Tal+Amn) reduces vendor prices by 15%.
Gheed's Fortune Grand Charm reduces prices by another 10-15%.
That 30% discount means 30% more chances at a payoff!

Guide.title: Crafting Masterclass: The 2/20 Amulet
Guide.description: The definitive guide to crafting Caster Amulets with +2 Skills and 20% FCR.
Guide.author: Nexus Team

content.heading: The Caster Amulet Recipe
content.text: The most sought-after craft in the game.
list: Recipe: Magic Amulet + Ral Rune + Perfect Amethyst + Any Jewel.
Fixed Stats: (5-10)% Faster Cast Rate, + (10-20) Mana, Regenerate Mana (4-10)%.

content.heading: The Level 93 Rule
content.text: To guarantee the CHANCE of rolling +2 Class Skills, your character level plus the item level of the amulet must be high enough.
list: Formula: Crafted iLvl = int(Clvl/2) + int(iLvl/2). We need result >= 90.
Strategy: Gamble amulets on a lvl 93 char (iLvl will be 88-97). Craft with lvl 93 char.

content.heading: Blood Gloves Recipe
content.text: Essential for Melee builds (Amazons, Smiters, Barbarians).
list: Recipe: Magic Heavy/Sharkskin/Vampirebone Gloves + Nef Rune + Perfect Ruby + Any Jewel.
Fixed Stats: (5-10)% Crushing Blow, (1-3)% Life Leech, + (10-20) Life.
Goal: Look for +20% IAS and +Skills (Java/Passive) on these.

content.heading: Hit Power Gloves Recipe
content.text: Critical for Bowazons who need Knockback.
list: Recipe: Magic Chain Gloves + Ort Rune + Perfect Sapphire + Any Jewel.
Fixed Stats: Knockback, 5% Chance to cast Frost Nova, Attacker Takes Damage.

Guide.title: Reign of the Warlock: New Items Mastery
Guide.description: An exhaustive guide to the new Grimoires, unique jewels, and class-specific runewords introduced in the ROTW expansion.
Guide.author: Cain

content.heading: The Grimoire: Warlock Exclusive Offhand
content.text: The Reign of the Warlock (ROTW) expansion introduced over 30 new items, but the defining addition is the Grimoire. This class-specific item acts as an off-hand shield (similar to Necromancer Shrunken Heads) and can roll innate Warlock staff-mods.
content.text2: Through their latent passives, Warlocks are uniquely capable of equipping a Grimoire while simultaneously wielding a two-handed weapon, vastly expanding their stat potential.
list: Ars Tor'Baalos: The ultimate Blasphemous Compendium. Widely sought for its massive minus to enemy magic resistance.
Ars Dul'Mephistos: An Occult Tome packing intense elemental and casting enhancements.
Base Types: Include Old Books, Burnt Texts, Forgotten Volumes, Tomes, Codices, and Compendiums.
content.tip: Grimoires can roll innate -Enemy Magic Resistance, which is practically required for taking endgame magic damage builds to the next level!

content.heading: New Unique Items & Jewels
content.text: Several newly forged unique items have been discovered that drastically alter endgame gearing strategies.
list: Gheed's Wager (Troll Belt): A high-stakes utility belt favored by wealthy adventurers.
Hellwarden's Will (Death Mask): A dark visage focusing on resilience and cursed power.
Entropy Locket (Amulet) & Sling Ring: New jewelry providing specialized stats.
Colossal Ancient Jewels: Dropped exclusively from the new 'Colossal Ancients' pinnacle encounter, these unique jewels are limited to one equipped at a time.

content.heading: New Runewords & The Authority Armor
content.text: The expansion introduces five new potent runewords that take advantage of the Warlock's innate abilities.
list: Authority (Body Armor): The premier Warlock runeword, providing massive bonuses to Warlock skills alongside unique 'chance to cast' protective effects that ensure survivability.

content.heading: Staff Mods on Daggers
content.text: Daggers have received an underground buff. They are now classified under caster weapons that can roll inherent +1 to +3 Warlock skills, opening up extremely potent, fast-attacking runeword bases for martial warlock hybrids.

Article.title: The Enigma of Enigma: A Design Philosophy Analysis
Article.subtitle: How a single runeword rewrote the rules of Sanctuary
Article.excerpt: In any discussion about the D2 meta, one word resonates with more gravity than any other: Enigma. By democratizing teleportation, Blizzard destroyed the notion of distance.
Article.content:
*By: Tyrael, Archangel of Strategy*

In any discussion about the *Diablo II* meta, one word resonates with more gravity than any other: **Enigma**. But to understand why this runeword transcends numbers and becomes an object of almost metaphysical desire, we must look beyond "+1 to Teleport."

### The "Original Sin" of Design
The addition of Enigma in Patch 1.10 wasn't just a balance change; it was a total rewrite of Sanctuary's topology. Before it, the game's geographical space mattered. Walls were obstacles; rivers were borders. By democratizing teleportation—previously exclusive to the Sorceress—Blizzard destroyed the notion of distance.

### Why is it Iconic?
1. **Paradigm Shift:** Enigma transformed slow classes (Paladins, Necromancers) into apex predators.
2. **Efficiency vs. Aesthetics:** It created the eternal dilemma: wear the armor you want, or the armor you *need*.
3. **Status Economy:** Having an Enigma in a *Superior Mage Plate 15% ED* isn't just about power; it's a statement of wealth and patience.

*Editorial Conclusion:* Enigma is arguably the most successful and dangerous piece of design in ARPG history. It solves a convenience problem but creates a utility monopoly that the game has never been able (or willing) to escape.

Article.title: Architectural Despair: The Geometry of the End Times
Article.subtitle: Why Act IV is the shortest but most psychologically devastating act
Article.excerpt: Act IV is purposely short. It doesn't want you to feel at home. Every map is designed to force brutal confrontations in narrow corridors.
Article.content:
*By: Deckard Cain, Horadric Scholar*

While Act I is about nostalgia and Act II about vastness, Act IV (Pandemonium Fortress) is about **claustrophobia in the void**.

### Strategic Design
Act IV is purposely short. It doesn't want you to feel at home. The fortress is small, the NPCs are few, and the "City of the Damned" is a labyrinth of rock and fire that serves to break the player's morale before facing the Lord of Terror. Every map here is designed to force brutal confrontations in narrow corridors, elevating the risk of sudden death (Chaos Sanctuary).

### Tyrael's Role
Here, Tyrael stops being a distant guide and becomes the only safe harbor in an ocean of desolation. This design reinforces the central theme of Diablo: the desperate struggle of a few against the infinity of evil.

Article.title: Off-Meta Alchemy: The 'Rift-a-Sin' Mastery
Article.subtitle: Why this underdog build remains an intellectual favorite for veterans
Article.excerpt: While the Mosaic Assassin dominates, the Rift-a-Sin represents a conceptual beauty in D2 build philosophy.
Article.content:
*By: Tyrael, Archangel of Strategy*

While the *Mosaic Assassin* currently dominates the speed-clearing meta, there is a conceptual beauty in the older, more intricate "Rift-a-Sin." Here, we analyze why this build remains an intellectual favorite for veterans.

### The Poetry of Chaos: Making Riftwork Shine
The build revolves around the *Rift* runeword in a Scepter, triggering *Frozen Orb* on striking. But the magic isn't in the damage numbers—it's in the **Action Economy**. By combining the Assassin's high-speed *Dragon Talon* kicks with the elemental proc, the player enters a "State of Flow" where positioning and frame-data matter more than raw DPS.

### The Design Lesson
Rift-a-Sin teaches players that efficiency doesn't have to be linear. It's an "Alchemical" build that uses overlapping layers of crowd control (Freeze, Confuse, Holy Freeze) to dismantle the chaos of Hell difficulty safely.

Article.title: The Merchant of Whispers: Ormus and the Tragedy of Kurast
Article.subtitle: How a humble NPC became a masterclass in environmental storytelling
Article.excerpt: Ormus speaks in the third person not as a quirk, but as a symptom of a mind broken by Mephisto's encroaching shadows.
Article.content:
*By: Deckard Cain, Horadric Scholar*

Ormus is often treated as a simple potion vendor, but his design is a masterclass in **Environmental Despair**.

### Lore vs. Function
Ormus speaks in the third person not as a quirk, but as a symptom of a mind broken by the encroaching shadows of Mephisto. His role in Act III isn't just to sell gear; it's to remind the player that even the most powerful mages of the *Zann Esu* are barely holding on. When he "identifies" your items, he isn't just reading stats—he's confirming that there is still magic in the world worth fighting for.
